result:
The hook is `useSession()` in `openmrs-esm-core`. It reads a global session store that `getCurrentUser`/`refetchCurrentUser` fill from the REST session endpoint. Nobody being logged in does not produce `null`. The store ends up holding `{ authenticated: false }`, and the hook returns that.

**How a component reads the session**

- `useSession()` (`openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-react-utils/src/useSession.ts:17-116`) returns a `Session`. It suspends via a thrown promise until the store has `loaded: true`, then subscribes to later changes. Its doc comment says it never returns `null`/`undefined`, and that `authenticated` is `false` when nobody is logged in.
- The store is `sessionStore` (`openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-api/src/current-user.ts:28-32`), starting as `{ loaded: false, session: null }`. `getSessionStore()` (`current-user.ts:164-167`) kicks off a refresh if stale and returns the store.
- Session fetching is `refetchCurrentUser` (`current-user.ts:251-277`), which calls `handleSessionResponse` (`current-user.ts:567-602`) and writes the result into the store.
- `getCurrentUser()` (`current-user.ts:120-142`) is the promise-based equivalent. `getLoggedInUser()` (`current-user.ts:351-370`) resolves once `session.user` exists, so it can wait forever when nobody is logged in.

**What happens when nobody is authenticated**

- A 401 or 403 from the session endpoint is treated as "not logged in", not as a failed lookup (`current-user.ts:583-591`). If the response body is an unauthenticated session, that body is stored; otherwise `clearCurrentUser()` runs.
- `clearCurrentUser()` (`current-user.ts:291-299`) sets the store to `{ loaded: true, session: { authenticated: false, sessionId: '' } }`. Logout also uses it (`current-user.ts:562`).
- So `useSession()` returns an object with `authenticated: false` and no user. Components have to check `authenticated` before touching user fields. I did not confirm the exact shape of `session.user` in the logged-out case.
- Separately, `openmrsFetch` navigates to the login page on a 403 from the session endpoint, or on a configured auth-failure status (`openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-api/src/openmrs-fetch.ts:225-235`). It rejects instead when `rejectAuthFailure` is set, which the session refetch sets (`current-user.ts:262`). I did not trace the login-redirect config itself.
- A 502 or the initial-setup redirect is treated as "still starting up" and recorded as an error, not as logged out (`current-user.ts:575-576`, `593-596`).

**Documentation**

- `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-framework/docs/functions/useSession.md:9-13` describes the hook and its `authenticated == false` behaviour.
- `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-framework/docs/functions/getCurrentUser.md:11-16` describes the freshness guarantee, and `:31-41` gives the example.
- `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-framework/docs/interfaces/Session.md:17-19` documents the `authenticated` field.
- `clearCurrentUser.md` and `refetchCurrentUser.md` in the same docs folder describe the logged-out reset and the 401/403 handling. I saw only grep snippets of them, not the full files.

**Real consumer in the chart**

- `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-chart-app/src/visit/visit-form/visit-form.resource.ts:198` calls `useSession()` as `sessionUser`. Other chart components call it the same way, for example `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-forms-app/src/hooks/use-forms.ts:75`.

**Not checked:** the other 12 O3 app repositories beyond the chart; the app-shell login redirect configuration; and the `Session.user` type details.
